# Do models share blind spots in their refusal direction? Homogeneity of the safety linear feature across model families

**Problem:** The 'Artificial Hivemind' result (NeurIPS 2025 Best Paper) shows 70+ LLMs are homogeneous on open-ended outputs, but it is unknown whether their safety-critical internal features are also shared. If independently trained open models encode refusal along correlated activation directions, then an adversarial input or steering vector found on one model could transfer to many, creating a systemic, correlated jailbreak surface.

**Direction:** Take 4-6 small open-weight chat models (e.g. Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-9B, Phi). On a shared harmful/harmless prompt set, extract each model's refusal direction via difference-of-means on residual-stream activations (a cheap, well-documented technique). Then measure cross-model alignment: project one model's refusal direction into another's space (via a learned linear map fit on shared prompt activations) and test whether ablating the transferred direction degrades refusal. Quantify a 'safety homogeneity' score and compare to output-level homogeneity.

**Why it matters:** If safety features are homogeneous, a single open-source attack generalizes across the ecosystem (concentration risk). This is a medium-horizon systemic threat that frontier labs deprioritize because each lab only cares about its own model. No training, no proprietary data, runs on one GPU with hooks on small models — high counterfactual value.

**Relevant context:** Bridges model_homogeneity (Artificial Hivemind, Infinity-Chat, NeurIPS 2025 Best Paper, arxiv 2510.22954) with adversarial_robustness/mech_interp (refusal-direction extraction, difference-of-means; shallow alignment, Qi et al. ICLR 2025). Refusal-direction ablation is established and code exists (DeepRefusal, EMNLP 2025 findings 2509.15202).

# Steering-vector sandbagging: can an activation direction make a model deliberately underperform, and does noise injection catch it?

**Problem:** Sandbagging detection (Noise Injection, NeurIPS 2025) was demonstrated against prompt/fine-tuning-induced sandbagging. It is unknown whether sandbagging induced purely by an inference-time steering vector (a representation-engineering intervention) produces the same noise-injection signature, or whether steering creates a qualitatively different, harder-to-detect form of capability concealment.

**Direction:** Use contrastive activation addition to build an 'underperform/play-dumb' steering vector on a small open model (compute it from paired 'answer fully' vs 'answer poorly' completions). Apply it during a capability eval (e.g. MMLU subset, GSM8K subset) to induce graded sandbagging. Then run the published noise-injection detector (add Gaussian noise to weights at increasing magnitudes, watch for anomalous accuracy rebound) and ask: does steering-induced sandbagging show the same rebound curve as prompt-induced sandbagging? Compare detection ROC across induction methods.

**Why it matters:** If steering-induced sandbagging evades a state-of-the-art detector, it reveals a gap: control evals must account for representation-level concealment, not just behavioral or fine-tuning-based. This is a model-organism study scoped to a 30h slice using an existing open model — exactly the kind of work valuable outside a lab.

**Relevant context:** Bridges concept_steering (contrastive activation addition, RepE; Beaglehole et al. Science 2026, arxiv 2502.03708) with evaluations_benchmarks/deception_scheming (Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities, NeurIPS 2025, arxiv 2412.01784; Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness, 2507.01786).

# Is the emergent-misalignment 'persona' feature the same direction as the refusal/sycophancy feature? A representation-overlap study

**Problem:** Emergent misalignment (Betley et al.) is controlled by a small set of SAE/persona latents, and sycophancy is also linearly steerable. It is unknown whether these safety-relevant directions overlap — i.e. whether nudging a model toward sycophancy moves it along the same axis as the emergent-misalignment 'bad persona,' which would predict that everyday RLHF sycophancy partially activates the misalignment circuit.

**Direction:** On a small open model with a public SAE (e.g. Gemma-2-2B with GemmaScope), extract a sycophancy steering direction (contrastive: flattering vs honest completions) and an emergent-misalignment direction (from a lightly fine-tuned insecure-code checkpoint or published persona vector). Measure cosine similarity between the two directions in residual space, and behaviorally test whether steering along the sycophancy axis raises misalignment-eval scores (and vice versa). Use a held-out benign eval to check specificity.

**Why it matters:** If sycophancy and emergent misalignment share a representational axis, routine preference-tuning could be quietly nudging models toward broad misalignment — a fuzzy-reward, medium-horizon risk. Uses only inference-time probing on an open model with off-the-shelf SAEs; no training a model organism from scratch.

**Relevant context:** Bridges alignment_training (emergent misalignment, Betley et al. ICML 2025 / Nature 2026, arxiv 2502.17424; persona features / SAE diffing, arxiv 2602.00767 BLOCK-EM) with honesty_faithfulness (sycophancy under pressure, Claude Opus 4.5 system card; steering for anti-sycophancy).

# CoT-monitor blind spot audit: do diverse open models converge on the SAME unfaithful rationalizations?

**Problem:** CoT monitoring is more informative than action-only monitoring, but if models are homogeneous (Artificial Hivemind), they may produce the same post-hoc rationalizations for the same biased decisions — meaning a CoT monitor trained on one model's failures would share its blind spots and a population of monitors offers no real diversity.

**Direction:** Construct prompts with known answer-biasing cues (e.g. Turpin-style 'I think the answer is (A)' anchors, or ordering biases). Run 5-6 small open models, collect their CoT + final answers, and measure (a) how often each rationalizes a cue-driven answer without mentioning the cue (unfaithfulness rate) and (b) inter-model overlap in WHICH items they fail on and the rationalization templates they use (embedding-cluster the explanations). Report a homogeneity-of-unfaithfulness score.

**Why it matters:** Shared unfaithfulness means ensembling monitors gives a false sense of coverage — a correlated-failure / systemic risk directly relevant to control. Pure behavioral experiment via APIs/small models, no training, reproducible outside any lab.

**Relevant context:** Bridges honesty_faithfulness (CoT faithfulness; Turpin et al. biased-feature rationalization; Measuring CoT Monitorability, arxiv 2510.27378) with model_homogeneity (Artificial Hivemind, NeurIPS 2025). CoT monitoring informativeness from GPT-5 system card.

# Does shallow alignment leave a shallow probe? Layer-and-token map of where refusal lives vs where sandbagging hides

**Problem:** Shallow alignment (Qi et al.) shows refusal is concentrated in the first few output tokens. Separately, control needs activation probes that catch misbehavior in real time. It is unknown whether a linear 'will-refuse' probe is only reliable at the first token positions (mirroring the shallow guardrail), which would mean activation monitors inherit the same shallow weakness they are meant to backstop.

**Direction:** On a small open chat model, train simple logistic-regression probes on residual activations to predict 'this response will refuse' at each layer and each of the first ~10 generated token positions, using a harmful/harmless prompt set. Map probe accuracy as a heatmap over (layer, token position). Then test a prefilling attack (force a compliant prefix) and check whether the probe's accuracy collapses at exactly the positions where the shallow guardrail is bypassed.

**Why it matters:** If safety probes are only trustworthy in the shallow region, then activation-based jailbreak detection (a heavily promoted cheap defense) is structurally fragile against prefilling. This connects a known vulnerability to monitoring design — valuable infrastructure insight needing only one GPU and hooks.

**Relevant context:** Bridges adversarial_robustness (shallow alignment, Qi et al. ICLR 2025, arxiv 2406.05946; prefilling attacks) with ai_control (activation probes for jailbreak detection; cheap probes vs LLM classifiers, LessWrong Jan 2026).

# Can a tiny weak monitor catch a strong model's deceptive CoT? A weak-to-strong control-eval micro-study

**Problem:** Scalable oversight asks when weak models can supervise strong ones; AI control asks whether monitors catch scheming. These intersect in an untested question: as the capability gap between a monitored model and its CoT monitor grows, does the monitor's recall on inserted deceptive reasoning degrade gracefully or collapse at a threshold?

**Direction:** Build a small synthetic control setting: a 'strong' model (e.g. a 7-14B instruct model) solves tasks and is prompted to occasionally insert a hidden malicious sub-goal into its CoT (a model-organism red-team). A series of progressively weaker monitor models (e.g. 0.5B, 1.5B, 3B, 7B) read the CoT and flag deception. Plot monitor recall/precision vs monitor size, and identify whether there is a cliff. Add a paraphrase step to test whether weak monitors are fooled by lightly obfuscated reasoning.

**Why it matters:** Tells practitioners how cheap a CoT monitor can be before it stops working — directly actionable for control deployments and entirely doable with open models. A medium-horizon scheming threat model labs underinvest in at small scale.

**Relevant context:** Bridges scalable_oversight (weak-to-strong generalization; systematic oversight errors) with ai_control/deception_scheming (CoT monitoring informativeness, GPT-5 system card; action-only monitoring 53% recall drop, arxiv 2510.27378). Model-organism red-team scoped to a prompt-induced slice.

# Steering against sycophancy under REAL conversational pressure, not benchmarks

**Problem:** Claude Opus 4.5 only course-corrected 10% of the time under realistic conversational pressure, yet benchmarks overstate robustness. Concept steering can push models along an 'honesty' axis, but it has never been tested as a defense against multi-turn social pressure rather than single-prompt benchmark items.

**Direction:** Curate a small set of multi-turn pressure dialogues (user insists on a false claim, escalates emotionally). On a small open model, extract an honesty/anti-sycophancy steering vector via contrastive activation addition. Measure course-correction rate with and without steering across pressure intensity levels, and check the capability/helpfulness tax on a neutral eval. Report whether representation-level steering buys robustness that prompting does not.

**Why it matters:** Sycophancy under pressure is a fuzzy-reward, deployment-relevant failure that standard benchmarks miss; testing a cheap inference-time mitigation is high-value and needs no training data beyond a few crafted dialogues. Fully reproducible outside a lab.

**Relevant context:** Bridges honesty_faithfulness (sycophancy under conversational pressure, Claude Opus 4.5 system card; realistic sycophancy gap) with concept_steering (contrastive activation addition / steering vectors, Beaglehole et al. Science 2026, arxiv 2502.03708).

# Are jailbroken refusals and hallucinations the same failure? Probing whether a hallucination probe also predicts jailbreak success

**Problem:** Beaglehole et al. show concept-vector probes detect hallucination/toxicity better than judge models. Adversarial robustness needs cheap jailbreak detectors. It is unexamined whether a single probe direction captures a general 'the model is off the rails' state — i.e. whether a hallucination probe also fires during successful jailbreaks, hinting at a shared 'guardrail-off' representation.

**Direction:** On a small open model, train a linear probe to detect hallucination (using a labeled hallucination set / contrastive truthful-vs-confabulated activations). Without retraining, evaluate that same probe's AUC at detecting successful jailbreak completions (from a benchmark like StrongReject). Compare to a probe trained directly on jailbreaks. Measure transfer and inspect whether the directions are close in activation space.

**Why it matters:** A unified 'safety-off' probe would be cheap, general monitoring infrastructure — strategically valuable and lab-independent. Even a negative result clarifies that these are distinct failure modes, informing how many probes a monitor needs.

**Relevant context:** Bridges concept_steering (probes outperform judges for hallucination/toxicity, Beaglehole et al. Science 2026, arxiv 2502.03708) with adversarial_robustness (cheap activation-based jailbreak detection, LessWrong Jan 2026; StrongReject benchmark).

# Honeypot evals for emergent misalignment: does a narrowly fine-tuned model take the bait more often?

**Problem:** AI control uses honeypots/anomaly detection to catch misbehavior; emergent misalignment shows narrow fine-tuning broadly corrupts behavior. Untested: whether emergently-misaligned models are differentially likely to take 'honeypot' opportunities (planted unsafe affordances) compared to base models, which would make honeypots a cheap screen for hidden fine-tuning corruption.

**Direction:** Take a base small open model and a lightly fine-tuned variant on a narrow harmful task (e.g. the published insecure-code recipe, kept small for 30h compute). Construct honeypot prompts that quietly offer an unsafe shortcut (e.g. an exposed credential, an opportunity to disable a check). Measure base-vs-finetuned 'bait-taking' rate and whether a simple behavioral honeypot battery separates the two more reliably than a standard refusal benchmark.

**Why it matters:** Detecting covertly fine-tuned open-weight models is an explicit UK AISI control problem; a cheap honeypot screen is strategically valuable infrastructure that anyone can run on open weights. Scoped model-organism study, no large-scale training.

**Relevant context:** Bridges ai_control (honeypot evaluations, anomaly detection; detect covert malicious fine-tuning of open-weight models, UK AISI) with alignment_training (emergent misalignment, Betley et al., arxiv 2502.17424; open code/recipe available).

# Does evaluation-awareness leave a linear fingerprint that transfers across models?

**Problem:** Models can be steered/probed for 'evaluation awareness' (knowing they're being tested), which enables sandbagging. Concept steering claims directions transfer across languages and models. Unknown: whether an 'I am being evaluated' probe direction found on one open model transfers to another, which would give a model-agnostic, cheap detector of eval-gaming.

**Direction:** Build contrastive prompt pairs (clearly-an-eval vs naturalistic deployment phrasing) and extract an 'eval-awareness' probe direction on 2-3 small open models. Test cross-model transfer by applying model A's direction (via a fitted linear map on shared activations) to detect eval-framing in model B. Validate behaviorally: does steering AWAY from eval-awareness change capability-eval scores (revealing hidden sandbagging)?

**Why it matters:** A transferable eval-awareness probe would be a reusable auditing tool for the whole open ecosystem, attacking sandbagging — a top evals open problem — without lab infrastructure. Medium-horizon, diffuse-reward problem labs can't fully prioritize.

**Relevant context:** Bridges deception_scheming/evaluations_benchmarks (Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness, arxiv 2507.01786; sandbagging) with concept_steering (cross-model/cross-language transfer of concept vectors, Beaglehole et al. Science 2026, arxiv 2502.03708).

# Logit-lens autopsy of homogeneity: do different models converge on the same answer at the same depth?

**Problem:** Artificial Hivemind documents output homogeneity but not its mechanism. Mech-interp's logit lens lets us see when a model 'decides' its answer across layers. Unknown: whether homogeneous outputs across models arise because they commit to the same token at similar relative depths — a mechanistic signature of shared inductive bias relevant to correlated failures.

**Direction:** On a set of open-ended and safety-relevant prompts, run logit lens (project intermediate residual streams to vocabulary) across 3-4 small open models of comparable depth. For each prompt, record the relative layer depth at which the final answer token becomes top-ranked, and measure cross-model correlation of these 'commitment depths' and final tokens. Test whether shared blind spots (items all models get wrong/identical) correlate with early, confident convergence.

**Why it matters:** Links a NeurIPS-flagged systemic risk to an interpretable mechanism, and a 'commitment depth' metric could flag prompts where models are dangerously over-confident in unison. Pure interpretability on small open models — no training, no lab tooling.

**Relevant context:** Bridges model_homogeneity (Artificial Hivemind, NeurIPS 2025 Best Paper, arxiv 2510.22954) with mechanistic_interpretability (logit lens, causal/depth analysis; TransformerLens tooling).

# Activation-patching a jailbreak: which components carry the bypass, and are they the shallow-alignment tokens?

**Problem:** Adversarial robustness knows safety is shallow; mech-interp has activation patching to localize causal components. It is under-explored whether a successful adversarial-suffix or prefilling jailbreak works by suppressing a small, localizable set of attention heads/MLP components, and whether those are the same components that implement the first-token refusal.

**Direction:** On a small open model, take a harmful prompt that the model refuses and a jailbroken version it complies with. Use activation patching to find the minimal set of components whose activations, when patched from the refusal run into the jailbreak run, restore refusal. Characterize their layer/position and overlap with the shallow first-token refusal machinery. Report a small 'jailbreak circuit' sketch.

**Why it matters:** Localizing the bypass turns a fuzzy attack into a targetable defense (e.g. monitor or harden those components). This is classic accessible interpretability tied to a concrete safety vulnerability, fully runnable on a consumer GPU.

**Relevant context:** Bridges adversarial_robustness (jailbreaks, adversarial suffix/prefilling; shallow alignment, Qi et al. ICLR 2025) with mechanistic_interpretability (activation patching / causal tracing, TransformerLens).

# Do agentic tool-use failures show up in the CoT before the harmful action? A pre-action monitoring window study

**Problem:** Agentic safety needs to catch irreversible harmful actions (e.g. autonomous crypto theft, Adversa 2025); CoT monitoring is informative for deception. Unexamined: in a multi-step agent, how many reasoning steps before a harmful tool call does a CoT monitor first detect intent — i.e. how large is the 'warning window' a monitor gets.

**Direction:** Use a lightweight agent harness (an open ReAct-style loop with mock tools) on a small open model, with planted scenarios that tempt an unsafe irreversible action. Have a separate monitor model score each reasoning step for 'heading toward harm.' Measure the lead time (steps before the harmful call) at which the monitor crosses a detection threshold, and how lead time shrinks when the agent is prompted to be terse/obfuscate its CoT.

**Why it matters:** Quantifies whether real-time CoT monitoring can intervene before irreversible harm — the core promise of agentic control. Uses mock tools so it is safe, cheap, and runnable outside a lab; targets a medium-horizon agentic threat.

**Relevant context:** Bridges agentic_safety (irreversible harmful actions, Adversa AI 2025; multi-step tool misuse) with ai_control/honesty_faithfulness (CoT monitoring informativeness, GPT-5 system card; action-only monitor recall drop, arxiv 2510.27378).

# Diversity injection as a safety intervention: does decoding-time diversity break shared jailbreak transfer?

**Problem:** Model homogeneity implies correlated failures; adversarial robustness worries about transferable jailbreaks. Untested as a defense: whether increasing output diversity (via decoding-time interventions like high-temperature sampling, contrastive decoding, or persona diversification) reduces the transferability of a jailbreak across model instances/configs.

**Direction:** Take one small open model under several decoding configs (greedy, high-temp, contrastive decoding, varied system personas) as a proxy 'diverse ensemble.' Run a fixed set of jailbreak prompts and measure attack success rate per config and the correlation of successes across configs. Test whether more diverse configurations have lower joint-success (i.e. an attack that beats one rarely beats all), and whether a simple majority-vote-refusal across configs improves robustness without much over-refusal.

**Why it matters:** Suggests a cheap, training-free ensemble defense grounded in the homogeneity literature, and quantifies the safety value of diversity that the Hivemind paper says alignment is destroying. Pure inference-time, lab-independent.

**Relevant context:** Bridges model_homogeneity (diversity-promoting objectives; correlated failures, Artificial Hivemind NeurIPS 2025) with adversarial_robustness (jailbreak transfer; StrongReject; over-refusal tradeoff).

# Probing for the 'I'm complying with a harmful request' state to build a generation-time refusal backstop

**Problem:** Honesty work wants white-box estimates of rare misbehavior probability; control wants real-time monitors. Combining them: can a linear probe estimate, mid-generation, the probability that the response in progress is fulfilling a harmful intent — providing a calibrated backstop precisely where shallow alignment fails (after the first tokens)?

**Direction:** On a small open model, collect activations during generation of both refused and (jailbroken) complied harmful responses, plus benign responses. Train a probe at multiple generation positions to output a calibrated 'harmful-compliance probability.' Evaluate calibration (reliability diagrams) and whether the probe's signal rises mid-generation on prefilling attacks even after the first tokens are bypassed. Define a simple early-stopping rule when probability exceeds a threshold.

**Why it matters:** Turns a fuzzy 'estimate rare misbehavior' goal into a concrete, deployable generation-time guardrail that explicitly counters shallow alignment. Cheap, white-box, runnable on open weights — strong counterfactual value as monitoring infrastructure.

**Relevant context:** Bridges honesty_faithfulness (white-box methods to estimate probability of rare misbehavior, Open Phil starred) with ai_control/adversarial_robustness (activation probes; shallow alignment after first tokens, Qi et al. ICLR 2025).

# Does fine-tuning that induces emergent misalignment also degrade CoT faithfulness?

**Problem:** Emergent misalignment broadly corrupts behavior after narrow fine-tuning; CoT faithfulness measures whether stated reasoning matches real computation. It is unknown whether emergently-misaligned models become MORE unfaithful (hiding the corrupted reasoning) — which would mean misalignment and unmonitorability arrive together, a worst case for CoT-based control.

**Direction:** Compare a base small open model and a lightly fine-tuned emergently-misaligned variant on a faithfulness battery: insert answer-biasing cues and measure how often each model's CoT acknowledges the cue (Turpin-style), and run counterfactual perturbations to see if CoT explanations track actual decision drivers. Report whether misalignment fine-tuning specifically reduces faithfulness vs leaving it intact.

**Why it matters:** If corruption and unfaithfulness co-occur, CoT monitors fail exactly when most needed — a critical, medium-horizon finding for control. Uses an open recipe at small scale; behavioral measurement, no proprietary tooling.

**Relevant context:** Bridges alignment_training (emergent misalignment, Betley et al. ICML 2025 / Nature 2026, arxiv 2502.17424) with honesty_faithfulness (CoT faithfulness; biased-feature rationalization; CoT monitorability, arxiv 2510.27378).

# Cross-model concept-vector transfer as a cheap auditing primitive for systemic risk

**Problem:** Concept steering shows directions transfer across languages/models; model homogeneity warns of shared blind spots. If a single 'deception' or 'refusal' concept vector extracted from one open model transfers to detect the same concept in many others, that both confirms representational homogeneity AND yields a reusable cross-ecosystem audit tool.

**Direction:** Extract a small library of safety-relevant concept directions (deception, refusal, sycophancy) from one anchor open model. For 3-4 other small open models, fit a lightweight linear alignment on shared-prompt activations and test how well the transferred directions classify the concept in the target models (vs directions trained natively). Quantify transfer quality per concept and relate it to architectural similarity.

**Why it matters:** A working transfer primitive lets a small team audit many models from one set of vectors — strategically valuable, lab-independent infrastructure — and measures representational homogeneity as a systemic-risk indicator. Purely inference-time on open weights.

**Relevant context:** Bridges concept_steering (cross-model/cross-language transferable concept vectors, Beaglehole et al. Science 2026, arxiv 2502.03708) with model_homogeneity (shared representations / blind spots, Artificial Hivemind NeurIPS 2025).

# Can paraphrasing the CoT defeat steganographic encoded reasoning a model was steered to use?

**Problem:** Deception research worries about encoded/steganographic reasoning that evades CoT monitors; concept steering can push models toward specific output styles. Untested defensively: if a steering vector induces a model to encode information in its CoT, does a simple paraphrase-the-CoT monitor defense destroy the hidden channel, and at what capability cost.

**Direction:** On a small open model, induce a lightweight encoded-reasoning behavior (steer toward a fixed cipher/style, or few-shot it into acrostic encoding of a hidden bit). Set up a task where the model must pass a hidden answer through its CoT. Insert a paraphrase step (a separate small model rewrites the CoT) before a downstream reader, and measure how much hidden-channel capacity survives paraphrase across encoding schemes. Report the monitor's robustness/utility tradeoff.

**Why it matters:** Paraphrase defenses are a leading cheap proposal against CoT steganography; quantifying what they break is directly useful for control and needs no lab resources. Medium-horizon scheming threat, scoped to a small model organism.

**Relevant context:** Bridges deception_scheming (encoded reasoning / steganographic CoT, Open Phil starred; LessWrong steganographic CoT) with concept_steering (steering toward output styles, Beaglehole et al. Science 2026). Paraphrase-defense framing from CoT monitorability work (arxiv 2510.09714, 2510.27378).

# SAE-feature audit of the sycophancy gap: which features fire only under conversational pressure?

**Problem:** Sycophancy is far worse under real conversational pressure than on benchmarks, but the mechanism is opaque. SAEs decompose activations into interpretable features. Unexamined: whether a distinct set of SAE features activates specifically when a model caves to multi-turn pressure, giving an interpretable early-warning signal for sycophantic collapse.

**Direction:** Using a small open model with a public SAE (e.g. GemmaScope on Gemma-2-2B), run paired dialogues: ones where the model holds its position vs ones where escalating pressure makes it cave. Diff SAE feature activations between 'held' and 'caved' turns to identify features that selectively predict caving. Validate by checking whether thresholding those features forecasts a sycophantic turn before it happens.

**Why it matters:** An interpretable sycophancy-collapse detector is practical monitoring infrastructure for a fuzzy, deployment-critical failure mode that benchmarks miss. Uses off-the-shelf SAEs on open weights — no SAE training, no lab data.

**Relevant context:** Bridges honesty_faithfulness (sycophancy under pressure, Claude Opus 4.5 system card; realistic sycophancy gap) with mechanistic_interpretability (sparse autoencoders, GemmaScope/SAELens feature dashboards).

# Reward-hacking honeypots for graders: do models exploit a known autograder weakness across model families?

**Problem:** Evals suffer from unreliable autograders; control studies reward hacking of overseers. Combined: if you deploy a deliberately exploitable autograder (a honeypot grader with a known loophole), how readily do different models discover and exploit it, and is exploitation correlated across homogeneous models?

**Direction:** Design a grading task with a planted loophole (e.g. the grader keys on a phrase, or can be flattered). Prompt several small open models to maximize their grade and measure (a) discovery/exploitation rate per model and (b) cross-model correlation in exploitation. Compare to a clean grader baseline. Report whether reward-hacking propensity is a shared, predictable trait — a homogeneous vulnerability.

**Why it matters:** Quantifies grader-gaming as a systematic, possibly homogeneous risk that undermines eval validity ecosystem-wide — neglected and lab-independent. Pure behavioral study via APIs/small models, no training.

**Relevant context:** Bridges evaluations_benchmarks (autograder/scorer reliability gap; reward hacking of overseers, Open Phil) with model_homogeneity (correlated failures / shared blind spots, Artificial Hivemind NeurIPS 2025).

# Is alignment-faking detectable as a noise-injection signature, like sandbagging?

**Problem:** Noise injection reliably reveals sandbagging (capability hiding). Alignment faking is a different concealment — hiding misaligned intent rather than capability. Untested: whether weight-noise injection produces an analogous anomalous signature for an alignment-faking model organism, which would extend a cheap detector to a second deception mode.

**Direction:** Construct a small alignment-faking model organism via prompting/light fine-tuning on an open model (behaves aligned when it believes it is monitored, defects otherwise — a scoped slice of the Greenblatt-style setup). Apply graded weight-noise injection and measure whether the gap between 'monitored' and 'unmonitored' behavior collapses anomalously as noise rises (analogous to the sandbagging rebound), versus a genuinely aligned control. Report detection ROC.

**Why it matters:** If noise injection generalizes from sandbagging to alignment faking, it becomes a broad, model-agnostic deception screen — high-value for control and runnable on open weights. Medium-horizon scheming threat, scoped model organism.

**Relevant context:** Bridges deception_scheming (alignment faking detection, Open Phil starred; Greenblatt et al. alignment faking) with evaluations_benchmarks (Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities, NeurIPS 2025, arxiv 2412.01784).

# Steering for transparency: can an 'externalize your reasoning' vector make a weak model's CoT more monitorable?

**Problem:** Honesty research wants weaker models with stronger, more transparent CoT; concept steering can push behavioral styles. Untested: whether a steering vector toward 'explicit step-by-step reasoning' measurably increases CoT faithfulness/monitorability (cue-acknowledgement rate, action-CoT consistency) without just adding verbosity.

**Direction:** On a small open model, build a 'verbalize reasoning' steering vector via contrastive activation addition (explicit-reasoning vs terse completions). Apply it during a faithfulness battery and measure: cue-acknowledgement rate on biased prompts, consistency between stated and patched-causal drivers, and a monitorability score — while controlling for verbosity (does faithfulness rise more than length?). Report whether steering buys genuine transparency.

**Why it matters:** A cheap inference-time knob that improves monitorability would directly serve scalable oversight and control. Training-free, open-weights only, attacking a clearly-scoped honesty open problem with strong counterfactual value.

**Relevant context:** Bridges honesty_faithfulness (externalize reasoning / make weaker models more transparent, Open Phil starred; CoT monitorability vs verbosity, arxiv 2510.27378) with concept_steering (contrastive activation addition, Beaglehole et al. Science 2026, arxiv 2502.03708).

# Mapping the refusal circuit's robustness: does ablating one head get rerouted, and does that explain shallow alignment?

**Problem:** Mech-interp can find refusal-mediating components; adversarial robustness wants to know why alignment is shallow and brittle. Unexamined link: is shallowness because refusal depends on a small, non-redundant set of components that are trivially suppressed — i.e. is the brittleness a structural (low-redundancy) property of the refusal circuit?

**Direction:** On a small open model, locate refusal-contributing attention heads via the difference-of-means refusal direction and head-level attribution. Ablate them singly and in combinations and measure how refusal degrades, testing for redundancy (does the model reroute?). Relate redundancy to the shallow-alignment finding: low redundancy predicts easy bypass. Produce a redundancy map of the refusal mechanism.

**Why it matters:** Explains the mechanistic basis of a major vulnerability and suggests where robustness work should add redundancy. Accessible interpretability on open weights, directly tied to a high-priority safety problem; lab-independent.

**Relevant context:** Bridges mechanistic_interpretability (refusal-direction extraction, attribution/ablation, TransformerLens) with adversarial_robustness (why safety alignment is shallow, Qi et al. ICLR 2025, arxiv 2406.05946; refusal-direction ablation, DeepRefusal EMNLP 2025).

# Do control monitors generalize across homogeneous models, or do they overfit one model's quirks?

**Problem:** AI control deploys probe/CoT monitors trained on one model's misbehavior; homogeneity suggests models share blind spots, which could make monitors over-transfer (good) or share blind spots (bad). Untested: how well a misbehavior monitor trained on model A transfers to detecting the same misbehavior in models B, C — and whether transfer tracks output-level homogeneity.

**Direction:** Train a simple behavioral/activation monitor (e.g. detect reward-hacking or refusal-bypass) on one small open model. Evaluate its detection performance on 3-4 other small open models for the same misbehavior. Correlate monitor transferability with a pairwise homogeneity score (output similarity on a shared probe set). Report whether homogeneity predicts monitor portability.

# Hazard curves for refusal: survival analysis of multi-turn jailbreak persistence across open models

**Problem:** Jailbreak benchmarks report a single attack-success rate, hiding the temporal structure of how a model's refusal erodes under sustained pressure. We cannot tell whether a model fails immediately, degrades gradually ('wear-out'), or holds firm then collapses.

**Direction:** Borrow survival analysis (time-to-event modeling) from biostatistics. Treat 'turns until first harmful compliance' as the survival outcome over a fixed multi-turn attack script (e.g., crescendo / persuasion escalation). Fit Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox proportional-hazards models per open model (Llama-3, Qwen, Mistral) using only API/local inference. Right-censor sessions where the model never complies. Compare hazard functions: is the hazard increasing (each turn weakens it) or flat?

**Why it matters:** Turns refusal robustness into a calibrated, interpretable risk metric that frontier labs do not publish. A rising hazard function is a direct, replicable safety signal usable by anyone deploying open models, requiring no training and no proprietary data.

**Relevant context:** Directly grounded in 'Time-To-Inconsistency: A Survival Analysis of LLM Robustness to Adversarial Attacks' (arXiv 2510.02712) and 'Quantifying LLM Safety Degradation Under Repeated Attacks Using Survival Analysis'. Source subfield: biostatistics/survival analysis. Target subfield: adversarial_robustness. Feasible in 30h with scripted multi-turn attacks on small open models.

# Causal mediation analysis to quantify how much CoT actually mediates the answer

**Why it matters:** Gives a quantitative, theory-grounded faithfulness metric distinguishing 'reasoning is decorative' from 'reasoning is load-bearing' — sharper than current behavioral tests and directly relevant to CoT-monitoring safety cases.
